content.comment_body: Hello. I have a [product_name] with [article_no] and two [product_name] modules, both with [article_no]. Four PT100 sensors are connected to the modules' inputs. Using [product_name] software, I expected these to appear as analog inputs 1-4. However, every AI shows a value of 1000. Could this be a hardware problem or is something else incorrect? Thanks in advance!

The value shown in the analog input reflects the A/D converter output. For these modules, each analog signal appears in the range 0-1000 units (0 meaning -50 °C, 1000 meaning 200 °C). If you are seeing 1000 units on all channels, it typically points to sensor connection issues, such as a broken wire or a short circuit. Can you provide details about the PT100 sensors—are they 2-wire, 3-wire, or 4-wire? How were they wired up? Is your module supplied with 24VDC? Also, what is the color of the RUN/STOP LED (red or green)?
I discovered the issue was wiring related. I was following an outdated manual, and the loop wire for a 2-wire sensor was placed incorrectly. Thanks for your help!

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered uniform readings across all analog inputs in [product_name] software while monitoring multiple PT100 sensors, suspecting a hardware fault. Community feedback identified incorrect wiring as the root cause, attributed to reliance on old manuals. Key user experience insight: wiring instructions and feedback mechanisms should be clear to prevent confusion, especially for less experienced users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect individual and accurate readings from each PT100 sensor in the [product_name] interface, along with clear diagnostics or support to help identify and resolve issues when abnormal readings occur.
